html:
Tubal Uriah Butler was a Grenadian born preacher and oil worker who led the oilfield strike and riots in southern Trinidad in June 1937. The unrest is a founding moment of the labour movement in the British Caribbean.

Workers in the oilfields near La Brea and Fyzabad struck over pay and racism. When police tried to arrest Butler, a crowd killed a policeman, and riots spread across the island. More than a dozen people died.

Butler was jailed, but the strikes led to legal trade unions and the Moyne Commission, which looked into conditions across the West Indies. The way led on to self rule and to Eric Williams. The day the strike began, 19 June, is now Labour Day.
sum: Tubal Uriah Butler was a Grenadian born preacher and oil worker who led the oilfield strike and riots in southern Trinidad in June 1937. The unrest is a founding moment of the labour movement in the British Caribbean.
